# valifetch

> Type-safe HTTP client built on native `fetch` with [Valibot](https://valibot.dev) schema validation.
> Like ky, but with built-in request/response validation and up to 1.75× faster than ky.

## Installation

```bash
npm install valifetch valibot
# Deno
deno add jsr:@haihv/valifetch
```

## Core concept

valifetch wraps native `fetch` with:
- Automatic JSON parse (no `.json()` needed)
- Valibot schema validation on request body, response, path params, and search params
- Full TypeScript inference from schemas
- Retry with exponential backoff + `Retry-After` header support, timeout, hooks, deduplication, download progress
- SSE (`responseType: 'sse'`) — returns `AsyncIterable<MessageEvent>` with built-in SSE frame parsing

## Quick start

```typescript
import valifetch from 'valifetch';
import * as v from 'valibot';

const UserSchema = v.object({ id: v.number(), name: v.string(), email: v.pipe(v.string(), v.email()) });

// GET — response type inferred from schema
const user = await valifetch.get('https://api.example.com/users/1', { responseSchema: UserSchema });

// POST with body validation
const newUser = await valifetch.post('https://api.example.com/users', {
  json: { name: 'John', email: 'john@example.com' },
  bodySchema: v.object({ name: v.pipe(v.string(), v.minLength(1)), email: v.pipe(v.string(), v.email()) }),
  responseSchema: UserSchema,
});
```

## Create a configured instance

```typescript
const api = valifetch.create({
  prefixUrl: 'https://api.example.com',
  timeout: 10_000,
  headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer token' },
  retry: { limit: 3, statusCodes: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504] },
});

const user = await api.get('/users/1', { responseSchema: UserSchema });
```

```typescript
// Custom retry predicate — true = retry, false = never, undefined = defer to
// statusCodes + methods. Consulted for every failed response and network error,
// before `beforeRetry`, always bounded by `limit`. May be async.
const api = valifetch.create({
  retry: {
    limit: 3,
    shouldRetry: async ({ reason, response }) => {
      if (reason === 'network') return true; // retry POSTs on network errors
      if (response.status === 409) {
        return (await response.clone().json()).code === 'STALE_VERSION';
      }
      return undefined;
    },
  },
});
```

## All HTTP methods

```typescript
valifetch.get(url, options)     // CancellablePromise<T>
valifetch.post(url, options)    // CancellablePromise<T>
valifetch.put(url, options)     // CancellablePromise<T>
valifetch.patch(url, options)   // CancellablePromise<T>
valifetch.delete(url, options)  // CancellablePromise<T>
valifetch.head(url, options)    // CancellablePromise<void> — no body; responseSchema is ignored
valifetch.options(url, options) // CancellablePromise<T>
```

## Parallel requests

```typescript
// all() — tuple of results, preserves element types, rejects on first failure
const [user, posts] = await valifetch.all([
  valifetch.get('/users/1', { responseSchema: UserSchema }),
  valifetch.get('/posts', { responseSchema: PostsSchema }),
]);

// allSettled() — never rejects; standard PromiseSettledResult per request
const results = await valifetch.allSettled([valifetch.get('/a'), valifetch.get('/b')]);

// Both return a CancellablePromise; .cancel() aborts every cancellable input
const batch = valifetch.all([valifetch.get('/a'), valifetch.get('/b')]);
batch.cancel();
```

## Key options

| Option | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `responseSchema` | Valibot schema | Validate + type the response JSON |
| `bodySchema` | Valibot schema | Validate `json` body before sending |
| `paramsSchema` | Valibot schema | Validate `:param` path replacements |
| `searchSchema` | Valibot schema | Validate query string params |
| `json` | object | JSON body (auto-stringified); request-only, not on `get()`/`head()` |
| `form` | FormData \| URLSearchParams \| Record\<string, string\> | Form body (plain object values must be strings); request-only — removed from instance options, not on `get()`/`head()` |
| `params` | object | Path param values for `:name` replacement |
| `searchParams` | object \| URLSearchParams | Query string; instance value is a default, per-request value merges on top (request wins per key). Explicit `undefined`/`null` on a request key removes the instance default for that key. Instance defaults are appended to any query string already in the request path, not merged into it. |
| `prefixUrl` | string | Base URL |
| `timeout` | number | Ms before TIMEOUT_ERROR (default: none — never times out; `0` also disables) |
| `retry` | RetryOptions \| number \| false | Retry config — `{ limit, methods, statusCodes, delay, shouldRetry(ctx) }` (defaults: `limit: 2`, `methods: ['GET','PUT','HEAD','DELETE','OPTIONS']`, `statusCodes: [408,413,429,500,502,503,504]`, `delay(attempt) = 0.3 * 2**attempt`s + 20% jitter, capped 30s) |
| `responseType` | `'json'` \| `'text'` \| `'blob'` \| `'arrayBuffer'` \| `'formData'` \| `'stream'` \| `'raw'` \| `'sse'` | Response format; per-call only, not on `create()`/`extend()` |
| `validateResponse` | boolean | Validate response against `responseSchema` (default: true) |
| `validateRequest` | boolean | Validate body/params/search schemas (default: true) |
| `throwHttpErrors` | boolean | Throw `HTTP_ERROR` on non-2xx status (default: true) |
| `dedupe` | boolean | Deduplicate concurrent identical requests; key is method + fully-resolved URL (`prefixUrl` + path params + merged `searchParams`, from raw pre-validation values), scoped per instance (each no-arg `create()` gets its own cache). Excludes headers/body/schemas — don't enable for calls that differ only by header/body, and avoid on non-idempotent methods (default: false) |
| `onDownloadProgress` | function | Progress callback `{ loaded, total, percent }`; not called for `responseType: 'stream' \| 'raw' \| 'sse'`; works at instance level too |
| `priority` | `'high'` \| `'low'` \| `'auto'` | Forwarded to `fetch` unchanged |
| `signal` | AbortSignal | Request-only — not on `create()`/`extend()` |
| `debug` | `true` \| `(event: DebugEvent) => void` | Structured lifecycle logging (request, response, retry, cancel) |
| `hooks` | object | `beforeRequest`, `afterResponse`, `afterParseResponse`, `beforeRetry`, `beforeError` arrays |

## Design notes (intentional, locked)

- `searchParams` (+ `searchSchema`) is the query option; `params` (+ `paramsSchema`) is the path option. `searchParams` mirrors `URL.searchParams` / ky — the stem mismatch with `searchSchema` is deliberate.
- No generic `body` option — use `json` (validated against `bodySchema`) or `form`. Native `body` is removed via `Omit<RequestInit, 'body'>`.
- `responseType` is per-call only (not on `create()`/`extend()`) because it changes the return type.
- `ValifetchError.cause` is `unknown` (matches the standard `Error.cause`); any thrown value can be passed through.
- Hook signatures are positional and ky-aligned: `beforeRequest(request, options)`, `afterResponse(request, options, response)`, `afterParseResponse(data, response, request)`, `beforeRetry(state)`, `beforeError(error)` — not unified into one state object. A throwing hook propagates that error as-is (no `HOOK_ERROR` wrapping) and aborts the request. `beforeError` only ever sees `ValifetchError`s.
- Entry-point rule: `valifetch` (`.`) exports the core runtime + core types; `valifetch/types` exports every public type (including `JwtRefreshOptions`, `MockCall`, `MockHandler`, `ValifetchMock`); `./error`, `./auth`, `./mock` are runtime subpaths. JSR publishes only the `.` entry — `auth`/`mock` are npm-only for now.
- `options(url, requestOptions)` — the HTTP-verb method is named `options` deliberately; its parameter is internally named `requestOptions`.
- `retry.shouldRetry(ctx)` receives `{ request, retryCount, reason, response | error }` (`reason: 'status'` → `response`, `'network'` → `error`, `retryCount` 1-based). Return `true` to retry even when `statusCodes`/`methods` would not, `false` to never retry this failure, `undefined` to defer to the built-in check. May be async; always bounded by `limit`; never consulted for an ok response; runs before `beforeRetry` (returning `false` skips those hooks); throwing aborts the request with that error. The context type is `RetryContext`, also the base of `BeforeRetryState`.
- Counter semantics: `RetryOptions.delay(attempt)` is 0-based (`delay(0)` = first retry); `BeforeRetryState.retryCount` and a `DebugEvent` retry `attempt` are both 1-based ("the retry about to be performed").

## Auth helpers (valifetch/auth)

```typescript
import { bearerAuth, basicAuth, jwtRefresh } from 'valifetch/auth';

const api = valifetch.create({
  hooks: { beforeRequest: [bearerAuth(() => getToken())] },
});
```

## Error handling

```typescript
import { ValifetchError } from 'valifetch/error';

try {
  await api.get('/users/1', { responseSchema: UserSchema });
} catch (e) {
  if (e instanceof ValifetchError) {
    if (e.code === 'HTTP_ERROR') {
      console.log(e.status);               // convenience getter for e.response?.status
      console.log(e.statusText);           // convenience getter for e.response?.statusText
      console.log(e.responseBody);         // parsed server error body — only populated on HTTP_ERROR (JSON object or plain text)
    } else if (e.code === 'VALIDATION_ERROR') {
      console.log(e.issues);              // convenience getter for e.validation?.issues ?? []
      console.log(e.target);              // convenience getter for e.validation?.target: 'response' | 'body' | 'params' | 'search'
      console.log(e.validation?.input);   // the invalid data that was validated
      // Request-side validation (target 'body' | 'params' | 'search') has e.request === undefined —
      // the Request doesn't exist yet at that point in the pipeline.
    } else if (e.code === 'TIMEOUT_ERROR') {
      // request exceeded timeout
    } else if (e.code === 'NETWORK_ERROR') {
      // fetch failed (offline, DNS, etc.)
    } else if (e.code === 'ABORT_ERROR') {
      // cancelled via .cancel() or AbortController
    } else if (e.code === 'PARSE_ERROR') {
      // Reading/parsing the response body failed — json, text, blob, arrayBuffer, or formData.
      // e.responseBody is the raw unparseable text (JSON reads only); e.cause is the raw thrown value.
    }
    // Boolean convenience: e.isHttpError, e.isValidationError, e.isTimeoutError,
    //                      e.isNetworkError, e.isAbortError, e.isParseError
  }
}
```

| `ErrorCode` | Thrown when | Fields populated |
|---|---|---|
| `HTTP_ERROR` | non-2xx status, `throwHttpErrors: true` | `request`, `response`, `responseBody` |
| `PARSE_ERROR` | body read/parse failed (json/text/blob/arrayBuffer/formData) | `request`, `response`, `cause`; `responseBody` (JSON reads only) |
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | Valibot schema failed | `validation: { target, issues, input }`; `request`/`response` only set when `target === 'response'` |
| `TIMEOUT_ERROR` | `timeout` elapsed | `request`, `cause` |
| `ABORT_ERROR` | `.cancel()` or signal abort | `request`, `cause` |
| `NETWORK_ERROR` | `fetch` threw | `request`, `cause` |

A `beforeRequest` hook may return a `Response` to bypass `fetch` entirely (e.g. `valifetch/mock`); that `Response` still flows through `afterResponse` hooks like a normal fetched response.

## Hooks: retry and error interception

```typescript
import valifetch, { stop } from 'valifetch';

const api = valifetch.create({
  hooks: {
    beforeRetry: [
      // Return stop to abort retrying; return a new Request to replace for remaining attempts
      ({ request, response, retryCount }) => {
        // Give up early on a second 429 instead of waiting out the backoff
        if (retryCount > 1 && response?.status === 429) return stop;
        // Tag retried attempts so the server can detect duplicates
        return new Request(request, {
          headers: { ...Object.fromEntries(request.headers), 'x-retry-attempt': String(retryCount) },
        });
      },
    ],
    beforeError: [
      // Chain error transformations: each hook receives the error and must return it (mutated or replaced)
      (error) => {
        error.message = `[api] ${error.message}`;
        return error;
      },
    ],
  },
});
```

`beforeRetry`: returns `stop` (exported sentinel) to abort retrying and treat the original failure as final; a `Request` to replace the request for remaining attempts; or nothing to proceed with backoff. Hooks run in order; `stop` short-circuits remaining hooks. It only runs for failures that are retryable under your `retry` config (status codes / methods / limit) — a 401 never triggers it. A hook that throws aborts the request with that error.

`beforeError`: receives `ValifetchError` and must return it — mutate and return the same instance, or return a replacement. Hooks chain (output becomes input for the next).

## Extend an instance

```typescript
const adminApi = api.extend({ headers: { 'X-Admin': 'true' } });

// Dynamic extension
const authApi = api.extend((opts) => ({
  ...opts,
  headers: { ...opts.headers, Authorization: `Bearer ${getToken()}` },
}));
```

## Callable syntax

```typescript
const api = valifetch.create({ prefixUrl: 'https://api.example.com' }).callable();
const users = await api('/users');                          // GET
const user  = await api('/users', { method: 'POST', json: { name: 'Jane' } });
```

## Debug mode

> Do not use `debug: true` in production — raw `Request`/`Response` objects including credentials are logged.

```typescript
// debug: true → console.debug('[valifetch]', event) for every lifecycle event
const api = valifetch.create({ debug: true });

// debug: fn → custom handler, full type on DebugEvent
import type { DebugEvent } from 'valifetch/types';
const api = valifetch.create({
  debug: (event: DebugEvent) => {
    if (event.type === 'request')  console.log('→', event.request.url);
    if (event.type === 'response') console.log('←', event.response.status, `attempt ${event.attempt}`);
    if (event.type === 'retry')    console.log('↺', `delay ${event.delay}ms reason ${event.reason}`);
    if (event.type === 'cancel')   console.log('✕', event.request.url);
  },
});
```

`DebugEvent` discriminated union — `type` narrows the payload: `request` (+ `request`) | `response` (+ `request`, `attempt`) | `retry` (+ `request`, `attempt`, `delay`, `reason: 'status'|'network'`) | `cancel` (+ `request`).
Child instances inherit `debug` from `extend()`; child value overrides parent.

## Testing (valifetch/mock)

```typescript
import { createMock } from 'valifetch/mock';

const mock = createMock();
mock.get('/users').reply(200, [{ id: 1 }]);     // permanent fixture
mock.post('/users').replyOnce(201, { id: 2 });  // consumed once, then falls through
mock.get('/users/:id').reply(200, { id: 1 });   // :param wildcard
mock.get(/\/posts\/\d+$/).reply(200, {});       // RegExp (tested against full URL)
mock.when('*', '/ping').reply(200, {});         // any method

const api = valifetch.extend({ hooks: mock.hooks }); // attach
await api.get('https://api.example.com/users');

const call = mock.lastCall();
// call.method, call.url, call.headers, call.body, call.searchParams
mock.calls();  // all recorded calls
mock.reset();  // clear between tests
```

Body values are always `JSON.stringify`-serialised. Omit body for a bodyless response.
Null-body status codes (101, 204, 205, 304) always produce a bodyless response.
Unmatched requests fall through to the real `fetch`.

## Subpath exports

```typescript
import valifetch from 'valifetch';                   // main
import { ValifetchError } from 'valifetch/error';    // error class only
import { bearerAuth } from 'valifetch/auth';         // auth helpers
import { createMock } from 'valifetch/mock';         // testing mock (test files only)
import type { ValifetchOptions } from 'valifetch/types'; // types only, zero runtime
```

## Performance (ops/sec, Node.js 20, fetch mocked)

| Benchmark | valifetch | ky | axios |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET + JSON parse | 106,373 | 68,443 (1.5× slower) | 36,613 (2.9× slower) |
| GET + schema validation | 95,703 | n/a | n/a |
| POST JSON body | 82,530 | 47,700 (1.7× slower) | 31,562 (2.6× slower) |
| 4xx error path | 67,548 (fastest) | 38,687 | 9,207 (7× slower) |
